inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 2,917,694k weighted average for diluted EPS, three months ended 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 Interim Report, Note 19, treasury-stock method; basic 2,898,791k). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, buybacks are nil since FY2025 and no non-SBC issuance is planned.
inputs.net_debt_basis: INDUSTRIAL net financial position, ex-leases. H1 2026 Interim Report p.47: industrial debt with third parties 23,656 less industrial lease liabilities 2,567 = 21,089 (capital market 19,827 + bank 623 + other 314 + accrued interest/adjustments 325). Industrial cash 31,217 + financial securities 604 + current receivables from jointly-controlled FS companies 993 + net intercompany receivable from FS 796 + net derivatives 77 + cash held for sale 4 = 33,691. Reported industrial NFP is +10,035 (leases as debt); adding back the 2,567 industrial lease liabilities gives +12,602 under lease treatment (B). Financial-services debt (28,406) and its receivables are excluded: SFS US / Banco Stellantis / Chinese captives fund their own books and their earnings are inside AOI.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Industrial free cash flow FY2025 (company definition, FY2025 AR p.73): OCF -4,650 less financial-services flows (-9,700) less industrial capex and capitalised R&D 9,090 plus disposals 591 less JV contributions 1,116 plus pension contributions 40. Consolidated reported FCF of -12,637 (OCF less consolidated capex) is NOT the right owner base: it carries the growth of captive-finance receivables, which are funded by FS debt that is likewise excluded from net debt. FY2025 is a trough year; the model is component-built from AOI margins, not extrapolated from this figure.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report Note 19, Share-based compensation: total PSU/RSU expense EUR73m FY2025 (EUR45m FY2024, EUR189m FY2023). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed and treasury-share purchases were nil in FY2025 and H1 2026, so the combined figure equals the expense. SBC is expensed within AOI (SG&A), which is the top of the EBITDA build, so sbc_pct_path is 0% to avoid a double charge; at 0.05% of revenue the house/street band collapses to a point (band_position null).
inputs.interest_income_note: Industrial interest income (FY2025 'Interest income and other financial income' EUR1,218m) is excluded from the flows by construction: the EBITDA path is built from Adjusted Operating Income, which sits above net financial income. The matching asset (industrial net cash) is credited once, in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: Nil in FY2025 and H1 2026 (FY2024: EUR3.0bn). Dividend suspended Feb 2026 (FY2025: EUR1,959m paid). The flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding; SBC is immaterial (0.05% of revenue), so the unfunded dilution is ~1.5m shares/yr against 2,918m.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in EUR; Euronext Paris quote in EUR (Yahoo meta currency EUR). STLAM (Milan) is EUR too; STLA (NYSE) is USD 1:1 ordinary share, not an ADR. No bridge needed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built, applied identically to all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows and the weights). 10y Bund ~2.8% + 5.5% ERP x auto-OEM beta ~1.4 = cost of equity ~10.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5% (BBB-/Baa3 since Feb 2026; hybrids priced at 6.25-8.25%), ~3.9% post-tax; target structure 75/25 equity/debt for a large investment-grade OEM gives ~8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. Market-cap weights at the current price would push the figure lower, which is the wrong direction for a stock at a 52-week low. No bear-case WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease principal paid EUR874m (AR p.17531) + interest on leases EUR84m = EUR958m = 0.62% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.6%. Industrial lease liabilities (EUR2,567m) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (reported NFP +10,035 becomes +12,602). The D&A driver is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 6,981 less ROU depreciation 702 = 6,279, 4.1% of revenue; H1 2026 run-rate ~3.4% after the FY2025 platform impairments shrank the asset base), so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Deducted once in the bridge at book (EUR450m, FY2025 AR). Flows are consolidated. Equity-method income (FS JVs with BNP/Credit Agricole, Tofas, DPCA, Leapmotor 21%) is INSIDE AOI and therefore inside the flows, so those investments are deliberately NOT added to the bridge (matching-asset rule).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping at year 5), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. DATA BREAKS: FY2014-FY2020 rows are Fiat Chrysler standalone (revenue ~EUR105-110bn, adj-EBIT 4-7%); FY2021+ is merged Stellantis. No growth statistic spans the January 2021 merger. FY2025 is a kitchen-sink year (EUR25.4bn of adjustments excluded from AOI: EUR6.6bn platform impairments, EUR9.1bn product-plan realignment, EUR4.1bn warranty estimate change, EUR2.1bn battery-JV exits, EUR1.1bn hydrogen) producing a EUR22.3bn net loss and -4.5bn IFCF; it is not a run-rate and the base year of the model is the FY2026 guidance year, built from AOI margin + D&A, not from FY2025 reported numbers. CORRECTION TO ANALYSIS JSON: the industrial net financial position at 30 June 2026 is +EUR10.0bn NET CASH (improved EUR3.3bn from +6.7bn at Dec 2025, mainly the hybrids), not -EUR10bn net debt as the Analysis JSON states. TIMING: Y1 = FY2026 compounds from FY2025 revenue while the balance sheet is 30 June 2026, so H1 2026's -0.9bn IFCF is counted in both; the ~EUR0.3/share double-count is left in as conservatism and will wash out at the FY2026 update. The post-June remainder of cash payments on the FY2025 charges (~EUR1.1bn of the EUR2bn guided for FY2026) and the post-tax employee-benefit deficit are debt-like bridge items rather than margin-path noise. Stated FY2026 guidance (H1 2026 report p.53): revenue mid-single-digit growth, AOI margin low-single-digit, IFCF improved YoY and positive in 2027, capex+R&D 6.5-7% of revenue; FaSTLAne 2030: EUR175bn revenue / 5% AOI / EUR3bn IFCF by 2028, EUR190bn / 7% / EUR6bn by 2030, EUR6bn cost run-rate by 2028.

equity_bridge.item: Hybrid perpetual notes (equity-classified, treated as debt-like)
equity_bridge.note: Issued March 2026 in three tranches, coupons 6.25%/6.875%/8.25%, first resets 2031-2034 (H1 2026 Note 18). They rank ahead of common equity for ~EUR330m/yr of coupons; the reported industrial NFP counts their proceeds as cash, so deducting the principal here charges them once.

equity_bridge.item: Remaining cash payments on FY2025 charges after 30 June 2026
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 guidance: ~EUR2bn of FY2026 cash outflows relate to H2 2025 charges, ~EUR0.9bn already paid in H1 2026. One-off; kept out of the margin path.

equity_bridge.item: Employee benefit liabilities (pensions, healthcare, OPEB) net of 25% tax
equity_bridge.note: Total employee benefits liabilities EUR5,312m at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 AR Note 20) x (1 - 0.25). Service cost is inside AOI but deficit funding is not (the company's own IFCF adds pension contributions back), so the deficit is a debt-like claim.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2025 EUR153.5bn to ~EUR198bn FY2035), a haircut of the FaSTLAne 2030 path (EUR175bn 2028 / EUR190bn 2030). Historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward anchor: see notes.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All 5-year windows cross the January 2021 FCA/PSA merger (revenue doubled inorganically) and are set to null. 3-year windows run FY2022 (post-COVID pricing peak: revenue 179.6bn, equity 72.0bn) to FY2025 (restructuring trough: revenue 153.5bn, equity 53.6bn after a 22.3bn loss), so revenue -5.1%/yr and equity -9.4%/yr measure peak-to-trough, not trend. EPS and owner-FCF 3-year CAGRs are undefined (FY2025 EPS -7.75; IFCF +12.9bn FY2023 to -4.5bn FY2025). Post-merger full window FY2021-FY2025: revenue +0.7%/yr, equity -1.1%/yr.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (IFCF less SBC) history, post-merger: FY2021 ~+6.0bn, FY2022 ~+10.7bn, FY2023 ~+12.7bn, FY2024 -6.1bn, FY2025 -4.6bn. The 2021-2023 figures were a pricing/mix peak (AOI margin 11.8-13.0%) that no scenario below assumes recurs; FCA standalone ran adj-EBIT margins of 4-7% in FY2016-FY2019, which is the mid-cycle reference used for the mature base case.

base.ebitda_margin_rationale: EBITDA margin = AOI margin + D&A ex-ROU + ROU depreciation (~0.5%). SBC (EUR73m, 0.05% of revenue) is already expensed inside AOI, so the SBC driver is held explicitly at 0% rather than deducted a second time. Implied AOI margin path FY2026-FY2035: 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5, 5.75, 6.0, 6.0, 6.0, 6.0. FY2026 2.5% sits inside 'low single digit' guidance (H1 2026 actual 2.1%, Q4-weighted H2 with Cherokee launch and EUR1.0-1.2bn net tariff cost). Reaches the 5% FaSTLAne target one year late (FY2029 vs 2028) and tops out at 6% rather than the 7% 2030 target: 6% is FCA's FY2017-FY2019 adj-EBIT run-rate and Stellantis FY2024 (5.5%), i.e. mid-cycle for a mid-pack OEM, below the 12-13% of the 2021-2023 pricing peak.
base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +5% (mid-single-digit guidance; H1 +9.9% YoY but Q3 shipments -1% with North America -12% on Cherokee changeover). Then 3.5/3.0/2.5 gives FY2028 revenue ~EUR172bn vs the EUR175bn plan and FY2030 ~EUR179bn vs EUR190bn; 2% thereafter (mature-market units flat, price/mix with inflation).
base.capex_rationale: Capex + capitalised R&D (IFCF definition) was 6.9% FY2024, 5.9% FY2025, 3.8% in H1 2026; FY2026 guidance of 6.5-7% 'capex and R&D' includes ~1.9% of expensed R&D, so ~5% capitalised. Rises to 5.75% as the 60-model FaSTLAne cycle and the USD13bn US programme build, holding a 1.75pp gap over D&A that matches the FCA/Stellantis 2017-2024 history.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax ramps 12% to 25%: FY2025 cash taxes paid EUR204m; large NOLs/DTAs from the FY2025 North American losses and the Italian patent box shelter the first years; blended statutory ~25% by FY2032.
base.wc_rationale: Auto OEMs run structurally negative working capital (payables > receivables + inventory): growth releases cash, contraction absorbs it. 5% capture on the revenue change is a deliberately modest positive; the same setting produces an outflow in the bear case's down years.

bull.narrative: FaSTLAne 2030 delivered roughly on plan: implied AOI margin 3.0, 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, 7.0, 7.25, 7.5 then flat (7% by 2030 as targeted, 7.5% mature on three-platform consolidation and ~80% utilisation); revenue EUR178bn FY2028 / EUR191bn FY2030, matching the plan. Capex settles at 5.5% as platform duplication falls away.

bear.narrative: Turnaround stalls and the cycle turns: implied AOI margin 1.5, 2.0, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5 then flat. FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance, FY2027 barely improves, then a 2028-2029 demand downturn (-4%, -3%) with continued US/EU30 share loss, tariffs structural at EUR1bn+/yr, EU CO2 penalties from 2027 and Chinese entrants pricing Europe. Recovery to only 3.5% AOI, i.e. FCA's weakest mid-2010s years. Capex cannot be cut below 5.5% without conceding the product cycle. Negative working capital drains cash in the down years.

scenario_narratives.base: Filosa's FaSTLAne 2030 reset works, slowly and partially. FY2026 is the guidance year (revenue +5%, AOI 2.5%, IFCF still negative after ~EUR2bn of restructuring cash); 2027 brings positive IFCF as guided; the EUR6bn cost programme, Belvidere/Toledo/Warren launches and HEMI mix recover North America to a mid-single-digit margin while Enlarged Europe stays thin on CO2 compliance and Chinese price pressure. The company reaches 5% AOI a year behind plan (FY2029) and matures at 6%, the FCA/Stellantis mid-cycle, never revisiting the 2021-2023 12-13% pricing windfall. Owner FCF ramps from ~EUR0.7bn in FY2026 to ~EUR5bn by the early 2030s (plan: EUR6bn by 2030). Terminal value bound by the 12x cap (3x mature EBITDA), consistent with how the market has historically priced volume OEMs.
scenario_narratives.bull: The plan lands on time. North America regains share toward 9% on Cherokee/Ram midsize/large SUV launches and the USD13bn US capacity programme neutralises tariffs; Europe's LCV leadership and B-segment BEV position hold; three global platforms carry 50% of volume and utilisation reaches 80%, delivering the full EUR6bn cost run-rate. AOI 7% by 2030 and 7.5% mature, revenue EUR191bn in 2030. Still capped at 12x terminal FCF: no multiple re-rating is assumed, only the plan's own cash flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2021-2025 pattern repeats: three more years of US and EU30 share loss, warranty and launch-quality problems on new platforms, tariffs permanent at EUR1bn+, EU CO2 penalties biting from 2027, then a cyclical downturn in 2028-2029 that negative working capital amplifies. AOI never exceeds 3.5%; owner FCF is negative through FY2029 and only ~EUR1.5-1.8bn mature. The EUR12.6bn industrial net cash (less hybrids, pension and restructuring claims) is what keeps equity value positive; no going-concern issue given EUR44bn industrial liquidity, but the hybrids' 6-8% coupons are a permanent drag on common holders.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the thesis rests on a turnaround the company has missed repeatedly since the 2021 merger (three straight years of share loss in both profit pools, the July 2026 cash/cost disappointment, ratings cut to BBB-/Baa3, dividend suspended), and the FY2025 kitchen-sink makes FY2026 margins hard to read. Not higher because there is no solvency question (EUR10bn industrial net cash, EUR44bn liquidity) and FY2026 H1 already returned to profit. Bull cut to 20%: it needs North American share recovery, the full EUR6bn cost programme, tariff stability and launch quality to all come through independently. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical, capital-intensive volume OEM valued on mid-cycle owner FCF built from AOI margins, not on FY2025's restructuring trough or the 2021-2023 pricing peak. Risk is carried in the scenario paths and a 30% bear weight, with a single EUR 9% WACC and a 12x terminal cap (about 3x mature EBITDA) so that no scenario assumes a multiple the market has not historically paid for this kind of business. The equity bridge credits industrial net cash once and charges every claim ranking ahead of common holders: hybrids, pension deficit, minorities and the unpaid restructuring cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin recovery: every 1pp of mature AOI margin is roughly EUR1.4bn of owner FCF and ~EUR5/share of base value; the base assumes 6% mature vs 7% plan and 3.5% bear
Cash burn before the turn: FY2026 IFCF is negative again and FY2027 positive only on guidance; the industrial net cash that supports the bear case erodes if 2027 slips
US tariff policy on Mexico/Canada-built vehicles (Cherokee from Toluca) and EU CO2 penalties from 2027 are policy variables outside management's control
Deferred tax assets: a further NA loss year risks DTA derecognition and a longer cash-tax shelter than modelled, cutting both ways
Captive finance (SFS US, Banco Stellantis) is excluded from net debt on the assumption its receivables fund its debt; a US auto-credit shock would surface there first
Working-capital sign: negative WC releases cash in growth years and absorbs it in a downturn; the bear's 2028-2029 contraction is where this bites
